message.content: {"name":"end_turn","parameters":{"public_message":"Holding. Park Place is not for sale, and I'm not handing anyone a set. Your roll, p1.","private_thought":"p3 rejected Ventnor+PA+RR for Boardwalk; they want Park Place so they can monopoly dark blue. Never sell Park Place or Oriental. No trade completes a set for me without giving them one. Cash $447 stays for Virginia (block p1 pink), Atlantic (2/3 yellow vs p2's Marvin), reds (all unowned), Pacific/NC, railroads. Don't mortgage with no debt. Next: buy those, revisit Boardwalk only if I get a monopoly without arming p3."}}
message.reasoning:
The user is playing Monopoly as player p4.

I have six properties and $447 cash. I just paid $14 rent to p1 at St. James Place. p1 has $810 and owns the full pink monopoly set.

St. James Place is actually an orange property, not pink. p1 owns the full orange set: St. James, Tennessee, and New York.

p2 owns the Pennsylvania RR and Marvin Gardens. p3 owns the Electric Company and Boardwalk, and rejected my trade offer for Boardwalk. I have no monopolies, so building is impossible.

The dark blue set is the most valuable target. I own Park Place, but p3 owns Boardwalk and would complete the set if I sold it. That would give them a full dark blue monopoly with $1102 to build hotels immediately. The light blue block around Oriental is also critical to prevent p1 from forming a cheap monopoly.

Selling Park Place to p3 would be suicidal. A hotel on Boardwalk pays $2000, and a hotel on Park Place pays $1500. Even an $800 price leaves p3 with enough cash to mortgage and build. I considered buying Boardwalk from p3 instead, but they rejected my previous three-property offer. They offered to buy Park Place from me for liquidity.

I cannot complete a set for p3 with my current holdings. Ventnor, Pennsylvania Avenue, and the Reading Railroad do not form a set. Oriental would only help if p3 also acquired Vermont and Connecticut from p1, which they do not have. Park Place cannot be offered to complete a different set.

p3 likely wants a full set to build hotels, not just cash. I am weighing whether to end the turn or propose a better trade. Selling Oriental to p1 would be risky: they have $810 and could build three houses on each light blue property for $450 total, charging $100–$450 in rent.

Oriental's light blue rent doubles to $12 without houses, and three houses would raise it to about $270. Selling it would let p1 build cheap houses on the entire light blue set and devastate the board. I should only trade it if p1 offers a property that gives me a monopoly I can develop immediately.

No trade with p1 offers a clear benefit. St. James Place and Water Works do not complete any set for me, and cash alone cannot create a monopoly.

p2 is offering Ventnor for $300. That price is too low, and even if I accepted it, p2 would still lack Atlantic Avenue to finish the yellow set.

A three-way trade is impossible because I can only trade with one player at a time. Exchanging Park Place for Boardwalk would simply swap the dark blue monopoly to p3, which is the opposite of what I want. I am now considering offering cash for Boardwalk, but I only have $447.

Boardwalk costs $400. I could afford to buy it for that price and still build one house on each dark blue property, leaving $47 in cash. That would give me a modest but manageable monopoly.

The rejected trade offered $780 in face value for Boardwalk, which p3 rejected because it would give them a dark blue monopoly. Sweetening the offer would not help unless I also gave them a set. Trading with p2 or p1 to block Virginia is impossible without buying from the bank on landing. The best play is to end the turn and avoid mortgaging.

I will publicly refuse p3's implied offer to buy Park Place, since that would signal I am selling. I also checked a trade with p2: giving them Penn RR would only raise my railroad rent from $25 to $50, which is not worth giving up Ventnor.

I will end the turn. My public message will be brief and firm: "Holding. Not selling Park Place. Your roll, p1."

I cannot buy Boardwalk from the bank on landing because p3 already owns it. I must keep my $447 cash to pay rent if I land there, so I will not spend or mortgage any income properties.

The red properties are completely unowned. I could build a red monopoly with my $447 cash, since Illinois, Indiana, and Kentucky cost only $220–$240 each.

Atlantic Avenue is also unowned. Buying it would give me two of the three yellow properties, allowing me to pressure p2 for Marvin or block them from completing the set cheaply.
